articles.title: AI coding agents generate more code, but not more software
articles.summary:
Anyone who has even tangentially associated with computer programming knows that modern AI coding assistants and agents can be incredibly efficient at generating huge amounts of functional code. But coders making use of those tools also know better than to trust the accuracy of that code, meaning substantial effort needs to be spent reviewing any AI-generated output.
A recent study of actual coding practices across hundreds of firms finds that human code review forms a significant “bottleneck” for the overall efficiency of AI coding tools, resulting in “little evidence that firms increase software output or reduce employment” by using them. Any efficiency increased during the actual coding phase, the study authors find, is “absorbed by downstream constraints in the production process”; as “the code review process significantly increases in length, pull requests are more likely to require revisions, and reviewers leave more comments.”
Cut once, measure twice
To come to these conclusions, Harvard University researchers Fiona Chen and James Stratton made use of aggregated analytics data from Jellyfish, which measures the granular output of engineering teams. That data encompasses 300 million individual “work events” (e.g., commits and pull requests) and issue management software data across more than 700,000 employees at over 700 relevant software development firms from 2021 through March of 2026.

articles.title: 390 Meter unter dem Meer: Wie Norwegen den längsten Unterwassertunnel der Welt aus dem Fels sprengt

Rogfast: Norwegen sprengt einen 26,7 Kilometer Tunnel unter die Nordsee
Es ist kalt, es ist sehr, sehr laut, und – wenn ich ganz ehrlich sein darf – ich fühle mich alles andere als entspannt. Außerdem ist meine Schutzbrille beschlagen.
Ich befinde mich etwa 300 Meter unter der Nordsee, in einer dunklen, feuchten Höhle. Es riecht seltsam. Und mir wird immer bewusster, wie viel Druck Millionen Tonnen Meerwasser direkt über meinem Kopf ausüben. articles.title: What's been driving Hawaii's lava fountains?
articles.summary:
In most cases, hotspot-driven volcanism is relatively sedate, with lava flowing down mountainsides slowly enough that people can walk out of its way. But in a number of locations—Mount Etna, Hawaii, Iceland—lava gets expelled in dramatic fountains that can reach several hundred meters in height.
Right now, we’re not sure what powers them. However, thanks to a recent set of eruptions at the Kilauea volcano, we have some of the best documentation yet of erupting lava fountains. In a recent edition of Science, researchers from the US Geological Survey describe what we’ve seen and compare it with what we might expect based on our best ideas about what powers these fountains of molten rock.
Years of fountains
With three active volcanic regions that engage in fountaining, there has been a steady flow of dramatic videos of red-hot molten rock spouting from the Earth. But Kilauea has had only three fountaining episodes since 1823, even though it’s the youngest and most active volcano in Hawaii. That activity has led to intensive study, and we have a good idea of the volcano’s structure. Previous work has identified a couple of lava residues within a few kilometers of the surface, and the volcano had 35 separate data-gathering stations set up on Kilauea, including “seismic, infrasound, geodetic, gas, and visual and thermal cameras.”
Following a major eruption in 2018 that partly drained one of the underground lava reservoirs, there were indications that it was being steadily refilled.…

Un cycliste adulte qui roule sans casque hors agglomération n’enfreint aucune règle nationale en France. En Espagne, c’est terminé depuis le 1er octobre : les dernières exemptions à l’obligation de casque ont disparu.
Une réforme pour les « usagers vulnérables »
Daté du 24 juin et entré en vigueur le 1er octobre, le décret royal 518/2026 réécrit une partie du code de la route espagnol. Selon la DGT, l’équivalent espagnol de la Sécurité routière, il définit pour la première fois les « usagers vulnérables » (piétons, cyclistes, utilisateurs de trottinettes, motards) afin de mieux les protéger. Cette catégorie pèse lourd puisqu’elle représentait 50,8 % des morts sur les routes espagnoles en 2024, d’après Motor16.
Hors agglomération, le casque est obligatoire pour tous les cyclistes, et les exemptions existantes sont supprimées. Elles couvraient jusqu’ici, selon la DGT, les longues montées, les raisons médicales et la chaleur extrême. Les professionnels à vélo, comme les livreurs, doivent en porter un en permanence, avec un gilet réfléchissant. Pour les trottinettes électriques, le casque est obligatoire et l’âge minimum est fixé à 15 ans. Sur route, l’automobiliste qui double un cycliste doit désormais ralentir d’au moins 20 km/h sous la limite, garder 1,5 mètre d’écart et, sur une route à plusieurs voies, se déporter complètement.
En ville, rien d’équivalent

articles.title: Batteries are now cheaper than natural gas turbines used at many data centers | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Battery storage is now cheaper than a type of natural gas power plant favored by many data center developers, according to a new report from Wood Mackenzie.
On every continent and in each of the 43 markets that Wood Mackenzie surveyed, four-hour duration batteries were less expensive than open-cycle gas turbines. The consultancy predicts that the cost of electricity from batteries will continue to decline while electrons from gas turbines will only grow more expensive in the coming decades.
The report lands as energy prices in the U.S. and elsewhere continue to rise, fueling inflation as data centers push electricity demand to new heights. Prices for gas turbines have been driven up by AI data center developers, which have been buying any model they can get their hands on. The effects have been more acute for open-cycle gas turbines, which are more readily available but less efficient and more expensive to operate.
Those turbines are often used by utilities as peaking power plants, which step in to generate electricity in periods of high demand. As prices for those turbines rise, it can raise costs for utilities, too.
Open-cycle turbines are simpler to make than closed-cycle turbines, but even they now take two to four years to procure. Waitlists for closed-cycle turbines now extend into the early 2030s. Both backlogs have been spiking prices for all new natural gas power plants.

Surfshark ‘proud’ to have backed Disinfo 2026 after governments pulled out under political pressure
The VPN said intellectual freedom remains crucial at a time when AI-generated content spreads misinformation
Surfshark has said it is proud to have backed Disinfo2026 after the EU’s diplomatic service, Canada and Lithuania pulled out of the event following political pressure.
On Thursday, the VPN issued a statement explaining its decision to continue sponsoring the annual event, which tackles disinformation and online deception, despite government sponsors withdrawing their support.
As further evidence of its commitment to intellectual freedom, the VPN – one of the best on the market – emphasised the importance of safeguarding the free exchange of ideas. “Open debate must never be silenced. It is essential for building a safer internet,” stressed the VPN.

Les chercheurs expliquent avoir découvert le logiciel malveillant grâce à leur technologie App Anomaly Detection (ce qui leur permet de faire la promotion de leur entreprise). Pourtant, elle installait et supprimait discrètement d’autres applications ; elle pouvait aussi s’accorder des permissions sensibles et charger du code à distance.
Bitdefender ajoute que Midnight Mimosa est implanté dans le firmware de smartphones Android d’entrée de gamme de différentes marques. Il peut être actif avant même que l’utilisateur configure son téléphone et on ne peut pas le supprimer comme une application classique. articles.title: A Cray-1 supercomputer replica from 30 "obsolete" Mac Minis
articles.summary:
The Museo de Historia de la Computación in Spain has unveiled a 1:1 scale visual replica of the famous Cray-1 supercomputer from 1976. Instead of sourcing expensive, cutting-edge tech to run the system, the creative team powered the project with 30 2012-era Mac Minis. Developed over 18 months, the project serves as a 50th-anniversary tribute to the Cray-1 and Apple’s founding.
Mac Minis from over a decade ago might not seem like the obvious first choice for building a cluster supercomputer, but when networked together, the developers can orchestrate the 64 active processing cores into a combined 1.3 teraflops of performance in their most recent tests. The museum reportedly achieved 1.5 teraflops previously using all 70 available cores, prior to one node going offline. Benchmarks were obtained using a custom matrix-multiplication Python script. Five PCs are quad-core i7s, and the remaining 25 are dual-core i5 models. Except for two units from 2014, the rest of the array dates to 2012.
The replica is a valuable tool for museum-goers to understand the shifts in computer architecture since 1976. The original Cray-1 used vector processing, applying a single instruction to multiple data elements simultaneously, whereas the replica distributes work across independent processors in a parallel cluster. The peak theoretical performance of the original Cray-1 was approximately 160 megaflops. What was originally a purpose-built research machine has been re-created with consumer hardware …

articles.title: The maker of non-text AI model Jev valued at $7.5B just weeks after launch | TechCrunch

TypeSafe AI, the developer of Jev, a new type of AI model that gained rapid popularity after launching just a few weeks ago, has raised $870 million at a $7.5 billion valuation. The round was led by Andreessen Horowitz, with participation from Sequoia and existing investor DCVC.
The massive fundraise comes as little surprise given Jev went viral almost instantly after its September 15 release. The startup claims that a third of Fortune 500 companies are already using the model, a remarkably swift adoption by enterprises.
Jev is based on a transformer architecture, but it is not a large language model (LLM). It doesn’t output text, but instead produces probabilities, or what the company calls “calibrated decisions.” What has users and large corporations so excited about Jev is TypeSafe’s claim that it works significantly faster and uses far fewer tokens than LLMs. The company positions its approach as uniquely suited for automating tasks rather than generating text or code.
“We have been super good at human language for four years, but it’s not useful for automation because computers speak a different language,” TypeSafe co-founder Diogo Almeida told TechCrunch last month.
Along with Almeida, who was previously a researcher at OpenAI, TypeSafe was co-founded in 2024 by former Meta research engineer Sasha Sheng and Erik Gafni, an engineer and entrepreneur.

articles.summary:
Friday, October 9th 2026
AnyPS5 Achieves Full PS5 GPU Shader Instruction Translation
A few weeks ago, we reported on an intriguing project called AnyPS5, which aims to bypass emulation entirely and run PlayStation 5 games natively on Windows and Linux. Today, the project reached a significant milestone by successfully translating 100% of the PlayStation 5 GPU shader instructions. This achievement means that the "Oberon" graphics processing engine within the PS5 has been fully decoded. All 1166 GPU shader instructions, based on the RDNA 2 GPU IP, are now covered under the AnyPS5 project. The project relinks PS5 executables into the host system's native format and reimplements the console's system libraries for dynamic linking, similar to Wine or Proton. Since the PS5 already runs on x86-64 Zen 2 hardware, which is similar to a modern PC, AnyPS5 skips CPU emulation and recompiles shaders into SPIR-V for Vulkan instead.
What is particularly interesting is that once GPU shader instructions are translated, all the system needs are PS5 libraries so they can be dynamically linked from a native PC port. This means the PS5 game will see the exact same system calls on a PC as it does on the console. However, the system libraries have not yet been fully translated, with current statistics showing 84.81% of system libraries translated. articles.title: Physical AI Needs a Neuromorphic Path from Sensor to Silicon - EE Times
articles.summary:
The physical world does not wait for a sampling clock. It changes, moves, touches, slips, and vibrates continuously, yet the information that matters is often sparse, unpredictable, and fleeting.
A robot needs to react when an object approaches. A gripper needs to know the instant contact is made or slip begins. Yet much of today’s sensing and AI stack still samples physical signals at fixed rates, turns them into regular data, and sends them to processors built for dense computation.
This mismatch becomes particularly acute in high-speed applications—from autonomous drones to industrial processes such as laser additive manufacturing—where relevant physical dynamics can evolve faster than conventional sensing and processing pipelines can handle.
Sampling fast enough to capture these dynamics produces massive data streams, much of which is irrelevant to the task, making real-time processing increasingly constrained.
Turning sensing into selection
The path from physical sensing to AI needs an intermediate layer—not to process more data, but to select the information worth moving downstream. Neuromorphic principles provide a natural foundation for such a layer.
Event-based sensors turn sensing into selection. They respond to change as it happens, encoding only events that carry new information. An event camera, for example, records changes in light at each pixel, capturing their timing and location without continuously sampling the scene.

articles.title: Neanderthal wooden tools from Spain found preserved in stone
articles.summary:
The Stone Age owes its name to tools that survived to our time. The material early humans worked with most, though, was probably wood because it is so much easier to process. Unfortunately, we know very little about Paleolithic woodwork because wood rots relatively quickly. But at Abric Romaní, a rock shelter in Capellades, west of Barcelona, mineral-rich water coated wooden Neanderthal tools in a limestone-like crust. When wood rotted away, it left behind hollow molds that faithfully reflect its shape.
In a recent Science Advances study, a team of Spanish archaeologists has cataloged 597 wooden remains from Neanderthal living areas dating from 62,000 to 40,000 years ago. They found spears, digging sticks, bark trays, parts of shelters, and a club unlike anything seen before, suggesting Neanderthals were likely much more than just Homo sapiens’ dumber cousins.
Beyond hunting gear
The oldest wooden artifacts we have are mostly weapons. They include spears from a German town called Schöningen, a spear tip from Clacton-on-Sea in England, and the spear found alongside an elephant skeleton in Lehringen, Germany. Most came from waterlogged sediments, where a lack of oxygen slowed decay.
The spears mostly give us information about how Neanderthals hunted. The findings at Abric Romaní are different because the finds come from a place where Neanderthals lived, slept, cooked, and made tools over the course of some 20,000 years.

La premisa. El registro arqueológico tiene un problema que reside en que la piedra y el hueso sobreviven al paso del tiempo, pero los materiales orgánicos perecederos, como la madera, suelen desaparecer sin dejar rastro. Esto hace que podamos tener una idea equivocada de lo que ocurría en aquella época, pero ahora este nuevo estudio supone un gran hito.

El milagro geológico. ¿Cómo es posible que hayamos podido estudiar restos de manera con una antigüedad de 40.000 años? Aquí lo normal hubiera sido que se terminara degradando, pero el agua rica en carbonato cálcico recubrió los objetos de madera formando tobas. Y esto es una gran noticia porque cuando la madera original se pudrió, dejó un molde exacto en la piedra con una precisión que ha permitido a los científicos observar las características biológicas de la madera.

World Mental Health Day: Rest in the Age of AI
On World Mental Health Day, Gurudev Sri Sri Ravi Shankar explains how AI, screen time and meditation affect creativity, mental wellbeing and human connection.
Some years ago, our attention span was 45 to 50 minutes. Today, it has reduced to just 47 seconds. There is a severe attention deficit today.
The increased use of screens has a big role to play in this. When we stare at a screen for too long, we blink less. That affects the freshness and creativity of our minds. People today have more experiences than their senses and minds can handle. They feel emotionally exhausted and inwardly lost.
The purpose of technology is to bring us comfort. If it becomes the cause of distress, its purpose is lost. Holding onto cell phones all day hurts the nervous system. But if you are free from stress, you will use technology for a good purpose.
AI can have three interpretations.
The first is the absence of intelligence. A lot of what comes on social media is fake and AI-driven. We have to move ahead in AI, but with awareness. We forget to recognise intelligence in nature, which is an absence of intelligence on our part.
The second is artificial intelligence. It can only reproduce what is already stored, not create something new. It challenges our intellect and creativity, and pushes us to do something original. No mires el contador, mira el vídeo. El razonamiento es casi de sentido común. Los locales eran enormes, las redes los mostraban llenos y los datos de consumo eléctrico no cuadraban. Para salir de dudas, varios técnicos de Endesa pasaron el asunto por su propia IA, que cruzó consumo y dimensiones y dictaminó lo evidente: por tamaño y actividad esperable, esos restaurantes deberían estar pagando bastante más.

Francis said the craft “was missing” from the first wave of AI production tools. He described generating episodes with them, then rebuilding every element by hand in a conventional workstation to get the result to broadcast quality.
The studio Caloroga built in response handles recording and mixing on 24 tracks, with a full plug-in suite. Video podcasts have their own multitrack editor, and scripts can be written in the platform or transcribed from a creator’s existing recordings. WhatsApp utiliza sistemas automatizados para identificar comportamientos que puedan representar un riesgo para la seguridad de la plataforma o de otros usuarios.

AI agents have made identity the front line of enterprise security. Agents now number in the thousands. El reporte también advierte sobre la velocidad de los ataques: el tiempo entre el descubrimiento de una vulnerabilidad y su explotación puede ser inferior a 24 horas. OpenAI told investors this week that it actually had $18 billion less revenue than the $68 billion it said last month. That knocked down the stocks of Nvidia, CoreWeave, Oracle and Nebius, among others, on Thursday.
Fifty billion dollars in revenue is nothing to scoff at, of course, but the market is all about expectations, and investors are growing increasingly wary — not least because some of the frontier AI model companies such as Anthropic may be getting a little pushback from their biggest customers. Google this week debuted its one-stop Gemini assistant that can act autonomously, generate code and complete work across any device, including web, mobile and desktop. La particularidad del servicio es que los reportes salen directo del modelo, sin que un humano los revise antes de enviarlos a los equipos de cada proyecto. Anthropic lo reconoce de forma explícita en su comunicado.
“Los resultados de este escáner de vulnerabilidades opcional serán generados íntegramente por el modelo, sin revisión ni clasificación humana”, escribió la empresa, y aclaró que eso implica que algunos reportes podrían ser incorrectos o inválidos.
El cuello de botella que motivó el cambio

La compañía admitió que ese proceso de verificación humana se convirtió en una traba. Por eso, ante el pedido de varios mantenedores de recibir todo lo que el modelo detectaba sin esperar la validación, ya envió cerca de 5.000 reportes sin revisar a quienes lo solicitaron.

Grand comme une fenêtre, le dispositif à base d'hydrogel a été testé avec succès dans la Vallée de la Mort, l'un des endroits les plus arides de la planète. Une piste sérieuse contre l'insécurité hydrique qui touche 2,2 milliards de personnes.

Le problème n'a jamais été son absence, mais notre incapacité à la saisir sans machines gourmandes en énergie. Cette forme, inspirée de l'origami, n'est pas décorative : en multipliant la surface exposée à l'air, elle accélère la capture de l'humidité. TypeSafe Inc., the creator of the Jev artificial intelligence model, today announced that it has raised $870 million in funding at a $7.5 billion valuation.

The company’s funding momentum reflects the surging popularity of its model: It has already been adopted by about a third of the Fortune 500.
When an enterprise application needs to perform a task using a large language model, it automatically sends a description of the task to the model. The LLM then responds with its output. That output often takes the form of natural language text. Applications must condense the natural language text into a structured, standardized format before they can put it to use.
Jev partly owes its popularity to the fact that it skips the latter step. When an application asks Jev to perform a task, the model generates structured output instead of natural language text. That removes the need for applications to reformat and condense Jev’s output before using it.
It supports just three types of requests. Applications can ask the model to answer a question with the equivalent of “yes” or “no,” pick an item from a list or generate a score. AOC Intros U27G4Z Dual-Mode 4K Fast IPS 240/480 Hz Gaming Monitor
AOC introduced a new 27-inch gaming monitor in China, the U27G4Z model features a dual-mode Fast IPS panel capable of 240 Hz at 3840 x 2160 or 480 Hz at 1920 x 1080. The monitor has a 1 ms GtG response time, a claimed 0.3 ms MPRT (Moving Picture Response Time), and Adaptive-Sync and NVIDIA G-SYNC Compatible certifications. Speaking of certifications, the AOC U27G4Z also carries VESA DisplayHDR 400 certification, with 350 nits in SDR mode and 450 nits in HDR mode. It has a 1,300:1 static contrast ratio and covers 99% of sRGB and 95% of DCI-P3. For connectivity, it offers two HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 2.1 and two USB 3.2 Gen 1 Type-A downstream ports, a USB upstream port, and audio output since the monitor does not feature any speakers. Display Stream Compression (DSC) is required for the highest-bandwidth display modes.
The AOC monitor also supports Picture-in-Picture and Picture-by-Picture, and gaming features such as crosshair overlays, shadow control, and motion-blur reduction through MBR and MBR Sync. The included stand provides the full range of adjustments, while the monitor itself also supports VESA 100 x 100 mm mounting. AOC lists the U27G4Z on its Chinese website as mentioned above, however, it has not announced pricing or availability in other regions.

articles.title: Dois antivírus no PC? Isso pode acabar mal, alerta veterano da Microsoft • Tecnoblog

Dois antivírus no PC? Isso pode acabar mal, alerta veterano da Microsoft
Raymond Chen, engenheiro da Microsoft, relatou um problema causado no Windows por dois antivírus que "brigavam" entre si.
O engenheiro da Microsoft Raymond Chen relatou um caso em que dois antimalwares entraram em conflito no Windows.
Nessas circunstâncias, um pode tentar interceptar funções do outro por considerá-las suspeitas, causando o “caos” no Windows.
A recomendação é utilizar apenas um programa de segurança por vez; o Microsoft Defender costuma se desativar automaticamente quando outro antivírus é instalado.
Se usar um antivírus é bom, contar com dois é melhor? Não é bem assim. Quem explica o motivo é Raymond Chen, o veterano engenheiro de software da Microsoft que há anos publica histórias de bastidores da companhia. Esta é mais uma delas.
Não é que todo mundo tenha o ímpeto de usar duas (ou mais) soluções de segurança similares no mesmo computador. Na verdade, o comportamento padrão é o de utilizar apenas uma solução e, quando houver necessidade de uso de uma nova, a anterior deverá ser removida.
Mas toda regra tem sua exceção. Pois bem, Chen relata o caso de um colega da equipe de suporte corporativo da Microsoft que se deparou com um caso do tipo envolvendo um cliente da companhia.

articles.title: Un câble HDMI à 50 € donne-t-il une meilleure image qu'un câble à 5 € ?
articles.summary:
Un câble HDMI à 50 € donne-t-il une meilleure image qu'un câble à 5 € ?
Contacts plaqués or, gaine tressée, promesses de couleurs plus vives : les câbles HDMI haut de gamme se vendent cher. À catégorie certifiée et longueur égales, un modèle premier prix affiche pourtant la même image. Le label de certification compte d'abord, la longueur ensuite.
Au rayon connectique, les boîtes se ressemblent toutes, sauf par le prix. L'une promet la "8K", l'autre des "couleurs plus riches", une troisième met en avant ses contacts dorés. Entre la moins chère et la plus chère, le prix est facilement multiplié par dix. Et quand on vient de payer un téléviseur 1 500 €, on est tenté de lui offrir un câble qui semble à sa hauteur.
Des 0 et des 1, rien d'autre
Le HDMI transporte de l'information numérique. La console ou le lecteur envoie une suite de bits, que le téléviseur reçoit pour reconstruire l'image pixel par pixel. Tant que chaque bit arrive tel qu'il est parti, l'écran affiche ce que la source a produit, et un câble plus épais ne peut rien faire pour les couleurs ou le contraste. À l'époque de la péritel ou du VGA, c'était différent : un mauvais cordon analogique délavait réellement l'image.
Quand la liaison numérique faiblit, on le voit tout de suite. Les ingénieurs parlent d'effet falaise : l'image reste parfaite tant que le signal est lisible, puis se dégrade brutalement. Près de la limite, des points blancs ou colorés scintillent (les « sparkles »), l'image saute, le son coupe par in…

articles.title: Meta prohibió los anuncios de TikTok en Facebook e Instagram: “No tenemos que publicar a un competidor”
articles.summary:
Meta prohibió que ByteDance, la empresa dueña de TikTok, pague publicidad en Facebook e Instagram, según confirmó un vocero de la compañía. La restricción rige en Estados Unidos, Canadá, Egipto, Indonesia, Japón, Tailandia y Vietnam.
La medida no se limita a los avisos directos de ByteDance, también bloquea campañas de terceros que dirijan tráfico hacia TikTok o hacia otras aplicaciones de la empresa china en esos siete países.
“No tenemos que publicar anuncios de un competidor cuyo objetivo es sacar gente de nuestras aplicaciones”, dijo el vocero de Meta Christopher Sgro a The Verge.
Agregó que declinar servicios promocionales a un competidor es una práctica comercial normal en cualquier industria y que la empresa seguirá compitiendo en calidad de producto y experiencia de usuario.
Cómo se desarrolló la rivalidad entre TikTok y Meta
El bloqueo de los anuncios llega después de que TikTok dejó de permitir que los usuarios incluyan en sus perfiles vínculos que abran o inicien sesión en otras redes sociales.
Esa decisión eliminó los accesos directos hacia Instagram que antes figuraban en las biografías de TikTok.
Bloomberg agregó que TikTok rechazó anuncios pagados por Meta en los que la empresa pedía a su rival sumarse a compromisos de seguridad infantil equivalentes a los suyos.
El cruce muestra que la disputa ya no se limita a declaraciones públicas, sino a decisiones concretas sobre qué publicidad puede circular en cada plataforma.

Ultra sells a warehouse robot called OP1 Operator. It resembles a humanoid robot attached to the end of a traditional robotic arm. OP1 Operator uses a pair of grippers in the shape of forklift prongs to carry out its work.
The robot has a vertical reach of up to 10 feet, which enables it to take merchandise off warehouse shelves. If an item accidentally falls to the ground, OP1 operator can pick it up.
The inbound shipments that a warehouse receives often combine many different types of items in the same container. For example, an electronics supplier might group together components that belong to the same laptop series. In such situations, warehouse operators separate the contents of the container into bins that each contain a single type of component. That makes it easier to process merchandise for shipping.
Ultra says OP1 Operator can automate the task. It can also perform kitting, which is essentially the opposite operation. In kitting mode, OP1 Operator mixes and matches items from different warehouse containers into the same parcel. That’s necessary when a shopper orders multiple items from an online store.

Oxide Computer raises $445M to step up data center rack production
Data center hardware startup Oxide Computer Inc. today announced that it has raised $445 million in funding.
Returning backer Eclipse Capital led the Series D round. It was joined by AMD Ventures, Riot Ventures, Jane Street, Atreides Management and USIT, which led Oxide’s previous $200 million raise in February.
Oxide sells a data center rack that combines computing, storage and network equipment in a pre-integrated package. It contains 24 hardware modules dubbed sleds. Each sled hosts an up to 144-core central processing unit from Advanced Micro Devices Inc. The CPU has access to about 1.64 terabytes of memory and up to 300 terabytes of flash storage.
Each sled’s core components are supported by a custom chip called the Oxide Server Processor. It’s responsible for optimizing operating temperatures inside the module. Additionally, the chip manages the flow of power and installs firmware updates.
The sleds in an Oxide rack are linked together by two switches. The switches use a custom routing protocol to create a continuously updated map of the rack’s internal network. If the map shows that a networking component is malfunctioning, the switches route traffic around it to avoid slowdowns.

articles.title: Xbox and PlayStation US Sales Sink as Average Console Prices Hit Record Highs
articles.summary:
Saturday, October 10th 2026
Xbox and PlayStation US Sales Sink as Average Console Prices Hit Record Highs
Xbox and PlayStation console sales in the US are having a rough 2026, according to new Circana data that analyst Mat Piscatella shared on Bluesky. For the year 2026 through August, Xbox hardware unit sales are down 33% year over year, while PlayStation units are 25% lower. That puts Xbox at an all-time low and PlayStation at its lowest point since 2013. As one might expect, it looks like pricing is the main culprit. Buyers paid an average of $529 for a new Xbox console this year, 26% more than a year ago, and $597 for a PlayStation, up 20%. Both are record highs for the US, and Piscatella says price sensitivity is becoming a real problem.
The decline follows a string of price hikes tied to the memory and storage shortage. Sony raised the PS5 Pro to $899.99 in April, Microsoft pushed the Xbox Series X to $799.99 on August 1, and Nintendo moved the Switch 2 to $499.99 in September, a hike analysts had warned about back in January. August itself was weak, with total hardware unit sales falling 15% to 559,000, the lowest August total since 2013. The Switch 2, however, remains the best-selling console of 2026 in both units and dollars. Piscatella said the US hardware market hasn't been "in a more precarious position since the early 80s." The analytics firm estimates that Gears of War: E-Day sold around 230,000 copies since its launch, with around 168,000 of those copies coming from Steam and 62,000 of them coming from Xbox. The end result is that, even though few gamers actually bought Gears of War: E-Day, Xbox accounted for an estimated $26 million in revenue, where Steam only garnered $11 million.

articles.title: Cryptomonnaies : la taxation lors du passage en stablecoin adoptée à l'Assemblée. Mais il reste de l'espoir
articles.summary:
C'est un mauvaise nouvelle qui arrive de l'Assemblée nationale, avec l'adoption de la taxation lors du passage de cryptomonnaies à un stablecoin. Mais il reste du chemin à faire pour que ça devienne une règle en France !
Les négociations autour du Projet de loi de finances (PLF) 2027 ont débuté, dans une ambiance qui a rarement été aussi rude, au vu des difficultés financières de l'État. Et il semble que personne n'échappera aux envies de taxation des députés, et surtout pas la cible toujours facible des cryptomonnaies. Car un amendement qui vient juste d'être voté va faire parler !
La Comission des Finances adopte un amendement du PLF 2027 taxant les opérations crypto-stablecoin
Voilà un amendement qui na va pas plaire à tout le monde ! En effet, l'amendement déposé par le député communiste Nicolas Sansu et imposant la taxation lors d'un passage d'une cryptomonnaie à un stablecoin vient d'être adopté en Commission des finances.
Avec cet amendement, tout passage d'une cryptomonnaie à un stablecoin comme l'USDC déclenche le calcul d'une plus-value. articles.title: Cuáles fueron los primeros celulares comerciales de la historia: top 6 de Nokia 1100 al primer Motorola
articles.summary:
Hubo una época en la que hablar por teléfono en plena calle parecía una escena de ciencia ficción. Hoy, los celulares permiten trabajar, estudiar, tomar fotografías y acceder a internet desde cualquier lugar, pero la historia de estos dispositivos comenzó con equipos voluminosos, costosos y con una autonomía limitada.
En poco más de cuatro décadas, la industria pasó de teléfonos que apenas permitían conversar durante media hora a los smartphones que concentran buena parte de la vida digital.
El primer celular portátil comercial fue el Motorola DynaTAC 8000X, que llegó al mercado estadounidense en 1983. Su desarrollo había comenzado años antes: en 1973, el ingeniero, Martin Cooper, realizó una llamada desde un teléfono móvil experimental.
Este dispositivo comercial pesaba cerca de 800 gramos, medía unos 25 centímetros de alto sin contar la antena y costaba alrededor de 4.000 dólares. Su batería necesitaba aproximadamente diez horas de carga para ofrecer hasta 30 minutos de conversación.
Aquel avance fue posible gracias al despliegue de las primeras redes celulares comerciales. Japón puso en marcha una red en 1979 y los países nórdicos inauguraron el sistema NMT en 1981. Desde entonces, fabricantes como Motorola, Nokia y Siemens compitieron por reducir el tamaño de los equipos y ampliar sus funciones.

articles.title: Citrix Patches Critical NetScaler Flaw That Could Enable RCE in SAML Deployments
articles.summary:
Citrix has released patches for yet another critical security flaw impacting NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway that could result in remote code execution or denial-of-service (DoS) under certain conditions.
"CVE-2026-107406 is a memory overflow vulnerability that may lead to remote code execution or denial-of-service under specific configuration conditions," Citrix said.
The vulnerability carries a CVSS score of 9.5 out of 10.0. There is no evidence that the issue has been exploited in the wild. Citrix has credited Michael Tucker, Chew Keong Tan, and Alex Bernier of the JPMorgan Chase XOR Team, along with Maxim Suhanov, for discovering and reporting the flaw.
Successful exploitation hinges on the NetScaler deployments being configured as a SAML identity provider (IdP) or service provider (SP). Customers can determine if their instances meet the criteria by checking the configuration for entries like below -
- SAML SP: add authentication samlAction
- SAML IdP: add authentication samlIdPProfile

articles.title: La chute des ventes d'ordinateurs s'accélère violemment ces derniers mois
articles.summary:
Le climat n'est pas au beau fixe pour le secteur des ordinateurs. Car les ventes reculent fortement ces derniers mois !
Le secteur de la tech est d'un côté dans une forme exceptionnelle, quand on regarde les activités liées à l'IA. Mais de l'autre, quand on jette un oeil cette fois aux ventes d'appareils électroniques, c'est clairement une autre chanson qui nous est jouée. Les ventes de smartphone sont ainsi en chute libre, tout comme celles des ordinateurs, ainsi que nous le rapportent les derniers chiffres de IDC.

En effet, on peut observer cette fois durant le troisième trimestre une chute très lourde des ventes, cette fois de -20,1% sur un an. Durant cette période, ce sont 62,7 millions d'unités qui ont trouvé preneur. Mais cet effondrement global cache des disparités entre les différentes marques que l'on peut retrouver en magasin.
Apple s'en sort mieux que les géants du secteur

Three research teams broke into Google's Pixel 10 on October 8 at Pwn2Own Ireland, a hacking contest in Cork whose rules require every target to be fully patched. The contest pays researchers to show working exploits and passes the flaws to the vendors. One of the three Pixel exploits earned Ikotas Labs $300,000, the contest's top prize, and made the team the overall winner.
Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative (ZDI), which runs Pwn2Own, posted the results but had not published how the three exploits work as of October 9. The wins were demonstrations on contest phones, and at least two of the three used a bug that was already known before the attempt.
The contest rules require each entry to use bugs that are not already known to the vendor or to the organizer. An entry that uses an already-known bug, which ZDI calls a collision, can still be accepted at a lower prize.
The three Pixel 10 wins, in the order they happened:
| Team | ZDI's Description | Award | Points | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Xint (Tim Becker and Yves Bieri) | Used "a single bug collision" | $150,000 | 15 |

While the figures have a small degree of variability, both agencies agree on one thing – the AI boom is responsible for the PC industry's problems, and it all comes down to the price of chips and other components.
High PC prices are driving down sales at an alarming rate
"The impact of upstream component cost increases has now fully worked its way through to end-market pricing," Omdia Research Director Ishan Dutt explained. DRAM and SSDs are the main offenders, Omdia explained, noting that their share of a total PC's price has risen from around 15% to 40%.

articles.title: GoBalance Flaw Lets Attackers Hijack .onion Addresses by Recovering Tor-Format Keys
articles.summary:
A bug in GoBalance, a tool many dark-web sites use to stay reachable during attacks, lets anyone work out the secret key that controls a site's .onion address using only public information, and then take that address over.
Searchlight Cyber, which disclosed the flaw on October 8, says an attacker who recovers the key can redirect the site's visitors to a copy of the site they control. Taking over the address does not grant the attacker access to the site's servers, database, or stored user data.
How the Flaw Works
An .onion address is really a public key, so whoever holds the matching private key controls the address. To stay reachable, a site publishes a signed record, called a descriptor, that anyone on the Tor network can fetch, and GoBalance signs that record.
The flaw is in the signing step. A Tor private key is 64 bytes long, but GoBalance passed only the first 32 bytes to the signer and dropped the rest. The dropped half is the part that keeps each signature's secret value hidden.
Without that half, the secret value becomes a fixed number anyone can compute. A single published descriptor then carries enough to recover the site's private key, with no access to its servers.
Because the exposed key is the site's long-term master key, not a short-lived one, a recovered key can sign valid records for the address far into the future.

Google shows off a whole new type of keyboard — and it says having keys rolling on a conveyor belt will make typing easier for all
It's certainly a new look for keyboards
- Google Japan's Gboard team unveiled a DIY conveyor-belt keyboard featuring 116 keys on four looping belts that move towards your hand
- Google pitches it at one-handed and one-finger typing, not "for all," and it is the 15th entry in a deliberately absurd series that began as April Fools' gags in 2010
- The design files are open source on GitHub, but only the motorized "Moving Keys" edition is documented, while the typing-capable Bluetooth edition and its board files are still marked as "coming soon."
Google Japan's Gboard team has unveiled the Gboard Conveyor Belt Version, a desktop contraption that mounts its keys on four looping belts so that characters scroll past a waiting fingertip.
Its Japanese name, the Gboard kurukuru version, means something like "round and round," with a nod to the word kuru, which roughly translates as "to approach/arrive".
Google has no plans to market or sell the unique contraption, but it has published the design files on GitHub under an Apache 2.0 license for anyone with a 3D printer and plenty of patience.

La startup de hardware Natura presentó Interface, un anillo inteligente de USD 99 diseñado para que los usuarios activen asistentes de inteligencia artificial con solo apretar un botón en el dedo, sin necesidad de mirar el teléfono.
El dispositivo se conecta con varios agentes de IA a la vez: Muse de Meta, Instinct, Grok Bot de xAI, Claude de Anthropic y ChatGPT de OpenAI. El usuario puede elegir qué asistente resuelve cada tarea, según informó TechCrunch.

articles.title: The AI Velocity Paradox: Why Security Is Decades Behind AI Ambition
articles.summary:
As enterprises race to deploy autonomous AI agents to accelerate business, a new report reveals they are tethered to security architectures built for a different era. The "Horizons of Identity Security" report from SailPoint highlights a critical “velocity paradox,” in which organizations invest in AI-speed business operations while continuing to rely on human-speed security controls, creating a structural failure that legacy approaches cannot solve.
The data shows that while businesses have spent years maturing their identity programs for human employees, those same playbooks are fundamentally broken when applied to the ephemeral, autonomous, and rapidly multiplying world of non-human AI agents.
A Market Stalled at the Starting Line
Despite years of investment in identity and access management, the market's overall security maturity has hit a wall. According to the report, the center of gravity remains firmly planted in the foundational stages, with a combined 60% of organizations still in Horizon 1 ("No Formal Program") or Horizon 2 ("Manual, Tool-Assisted").
The multi-year persistence of this trend reveals a critical insight: the problem isn't a lack of effort, but an architectural ceiling. The operational playbooks built to govern human employees may not scale effectively to govern autonomous agents executing thousands of transactions per minute.

Se trata de nueva consecuencia de la actual crisis de memoria generada por el auge de la inteligencia artificial.
IDC midió 62,7 millones de unidades despachadas entre julio y septiembre, contra 78,5 millones un año antes. El retroceso también fue de 9,1% respecto del segundo trimestre de 2026, algo inusual porque el tercer trimestre suele superar al segundo por estacionalidad.

Por qué se frenó el mercado
Jitesh Ubrani, director de investigación de dispositivos de consumo de IDC, explicó que buena parte de la caída responde a compras adelantadas que los fabricantes y los canales de venta hicieron a comienzos de año para anticiparse a las subas de precio de la memoria. Esa estrategia infló los envíos del primer semestre y dejó al tercer trimestre con poca demanda real para sostener. “Los canales ahora están preocupados por cargar demasiado inventario en un mercado donde los precios altos frenan la demanda”, dijo Ubrani.

articles.title: Google presenta teclado para escribir con una mano: sus botones se desplazan sobre una cinta transportadora
articles.summary:
La división japonesa de Google presentó un teclado experimental que invierte la lógica tradicional de escritura: en lugar de que el usuario mueva los dedos hacia las teclas, son las teclas las que se desplazan hacia el dedo. El dispositivo, bautizado Gboard Conveyor Belt Version, monta sus botones sobre cuatro cintas transportadoras que giran en bucle hasta que el carácter deseado llega frente al usuario.
El nombre original en japonés, Gboard kurukuru version, hace referencia a la palabra kuru, que se traduce aproximadamente como “acercarse o llegar”, y alude al movimiento circular y repetitivo de las cintas. El equipo de Gboard explicó que la idea parte de una observación simple: los teclados convencionales están diseñados para dos manos, por lo que escribir con una sola mano o un solo dedo obliga a desplazar todo el brazo y la palma por la superficie del dispositivo.
Cuatro cintas con 29 teclas cada una
El diseño distribuye 116 teclas en total, repartidas en cuatro bandas con 29 caracteres cada una. El usuario presiona el carácter en el momento exacto en que pasa frente a su dedo. A diferencia de los teclados tradicionales, las mayúsculas y minúsculas tienen botones separados, sin necesidad de recurrir a la tecla Shift, una decisión que la compañía considera más intuitiva para este formato.

articles.title: Researchers Publish Working Exploit for Pre-Auth AnyDesk Linux Flaw That Gives Root Access
articles.summary:
Security researchers have published a full working exploit for a pre-authentication remote code execution flaw in AnyDesk Linux that gives attackers root access before anyone approves the connection.
AnyDesk patched the flaw in version 8.0.3 in June, but its changelog described the fix only as "fixed a bug that could lead to a crash," with no CVE assigned and no security advisory.
The exploit, called AnyPwn, targets a heap buffer overflow in AnyDesk's session protocol, a remote desktop tool. The code was released on GitHub on October 8.
Administrators should update AnyDesk Linux to at least version 8.0.3. The latest release is 8.1.0.
What the Exploit Demonstrates
The published exploit works only over direct TCP connections on port 7070.
The exploit is probabilistic: the heap layout must place a target object adjacent to the overflowed buffer; otherwise, the service crashes instead of executing the attacker's command. The offsets in the published code target a specific build of AnyDesk Linux, 8.0.2; other builds would require different values.
The researchers say the same vulnerable code path is also reachable via AnyDesk's relay servers, which the software uses when a direct connection is unavailable. They validated this with a Frida instrumentation trigger but did not demonstrate the full exploit chain over relays.

articles.title: P7 DarkSword iOS Exploit Kit Adds Crypto Wallet Data Theft and Remote Commands

Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of a previously unseen variant of the DarkSword iOS exploit kit called P7 DarkSword.
"Compared with the variants we usually observe, P7 reduces its on-device footprint, adds on-device keychain and crypto-wallet theft, and adds two way C2 communication with the attacker's infrastructure," iVerify said in a new report published Thursday.
The name "P7" is a nod to the threat actor's use of the "p7_" variable prefix in changes made to the original DarkSword code.
DarkSword was first publicly documented earlier this March by Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG), iVerify, and Lookout, detailing its ability to target iPhones running iOS versions between iOS 18.4 and 18.7. The kit was detected in the wild in November 2025.
The toolkit is engineered to chain multiple iOS vulnerabilities to escape the browser sandbox, escalate to kernel privileges, and inject the main payload into SpringBoard, the iOS process that handles app launches and the home screen. The exploit chain is assessed to be a commercial product that somehow landed in a second-hand market, from where it was acquired by financially motivated operators and other threat actors since late 2025.

Et il est vrai qu’une infrastructure étendue présente de sérieux avantages. Sauf que le nombre de serveurs est avant tout une donnée d’inventaire, pas un résultat de test. Et pour comparer deux inventaires, il faut déjà savoir ce qu’ils recouvrent.
Des milliers de serveurs VPN, qu’est-ce qu’on compte au juste ?
Lorsqu’un fournisseur annonce disposer de plusieurs milliers de serveurs, on imagine assez naturellement autant de machines alignées dans des centres de données aux quatre coins du monde. Ce n’est pas nécessairement faux, mais le terme de serveur ne désigne pas toujours un équipement physique distinct.
